name: New Brunswick
summary: A gold lion on red in the upper third, above an ancient galley with oars on blue and white waves on gold. It is a banner of the arms granted in 1868.
origin: The arms were granted by Queen Victoria in 1868. The flag, a banner of the arms, was adopted on 24 February 1965.

symbols.name: Gold lion
symbols.description: A lion passant guardant on red.
symbols.meaning: New Brunswick's ties to Brunswick (Germany) and to King George III, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg.

symbols.name: Ancient galley
symbols.description: A ship with oars on waves.
symbols.meaning: Shipbuilding and seafaring, important to the province's economy.

facts: The province is named after the House of Brunswick, the British royal family of the time.
It is Canada's only officially bilingual province.
The galley recalls the province's 19th-century shipbuilding industry.
clues: A gold lion on red above an oared ship on waves.
